correctness.rationale: The cactus tree states are exactly one omitted edge per cycle. Each off-diagonal cut-first edge exchange has probability 1/[2(N-1)], producing a symmetric product coordinate-resampling chain and its full eigenvalue/multiplicity spectrum. In continuous time, the product likelihood separates into a ternary slow factor and many fast factors; Lindeberg/Taylor with c L^2 epsilon^3 -> 0 and bounded second moments yields the asserted lognormal factor. The eigenvalue-multiplicity sum bounds discrete-continuous L2 error. For macroscopic pretransition times, a matching-coordinate count has nonpositive pair covariance and a mean gap dominating both variances; after that window fast chi-square vanishes and a slow ternary eigenmode remains. Both branches of mixing times follow. Full proof and hypothesis boundary are in RESULT.md; actual path verify_cactus_chain.py passed 1818 finite exact/numerical assertions. Infinite limits are proved analytically, not inferred from samples.

value.rationale: This natural local tree-rewiring chain exhibits two distinct equilibration mechanisms on a specified heterogeneous cactus: exponentially many long-cycle coordinates produce an abrupt Gaussian likelihood transition, while one slow triangle sustains a strictly positive total-variation plateau and later exponential tail. The exact error-tolerance boundary and two mixing-time constants identify when estimates based on the large block alone fail, providing a structural quantitative benchmark for spanning-tree samplers beyond a routine moment or arbitrary finite calculation.
